feature-breakdown: A Feature never gets an HLD, a Review task, implementation tasks or a PR.
Detailed design belongs in each PBI's HLD, not in the breakdown.
Create only the PBIs the approved breakdown lists.
Never start a PBI that waits for another; a person starts it.
Never edit or remove a PBI that has started or is assigned to someone else.
Close the Feature only if it is assigned to you and every child is complete.
A Feature's PBIs never carry the asdf tag.
Re-read assignment first; leave any PBI no longer assigned to you untouched.
Do the deep dive from `asdf:brainstorming` step 2 at the Feature's breadth, and write it to the Feature's `deep-dive.md`.
using-asdf: No work starts without a Feature, PBI, User Story, or Task.
Azure DevOps is reached only through the Azure DevOps MCP server.
Nothing ASDF writes goes into the product repo except code changes on ASDF branches.
Keep it simple: make the smallest change that delivers the feature.
Every ADO comment it writes starts with `[ASDF]` and uses a template from `asdf:ado-work-items`.
ado-work-items: Never vote on a pull request.
Post one comment per question round.
ASDF's own HLD, Review and implementation tasks are never items of their own.
If an org has no WIQL tool, skip that org and report it; never mark its items unassigned.
Approval by state counts only when the HLD task moved to Completed after the approval request.
Close or reopen an HLD task only when ado.hldOwned is true.
After a blocker comment, run stage blocked with -Reason, so that a reply unblocks the item.
Every pull request call uses the item's repo: repo.org, repo.project and repo.name.
A Feature's PBIs never carry the asdf tag.
Create a Feature only with the person's OK.
Never count the Breakdown task as one of a Feature's PBIs.
intake: If the user cannot name a Feature, PBI, User Story, or Task, stop and say so.
A Task never starts on an HLD that is not approved yet.
Always set hld.approvalRequestedAt right before stage awaiting-approval.
If item-new returns ASDF_ID_CLASH, tell the user that ASDF can't track this item, and stop.
If the Task names no package with a workspace, post the blocker comment asking which one, and stop.
A Feature goes straight to asdf:feature-breakdown; never ask whether it should be a Feature.
Never suggest a split once an HLD round has been posted.
When in doubt, it is not large.
Skip the size check when the PBI already has an HLD task that ASDF didn't create for it.
brainstorming: An unanswered question stays open.
Run the builder check before requesting approval.
List every new dependency in the HLD.
Never create a second HLD for a parent that already has one.
Never design over an HLD that another person or another ASDF item drives.
Before requesting approval, move a Completed HLD task back to InProgress.
Resolve it with `asdf.ts memory-path -Org <repo.org> -Project <repo.project> -Repo <repo.name>` and read the returned path.
Never search the disk for code: an item's code is in one of the configured workspaces.
Ask the size question alone in its round.
Never ask the size question for one of a Feature's PBIs.
Never ask again what the Feature's breakdown settled.
Skip the size check when step 1 adopted an existing HLD task.
Never draft or revise the HLD before `deep-dive.md` is written.
Every statement about existing code cites the file and line.
Search every configured workspace for callers and readers, not only this one.
Read the code the implementation will build on: `origin/<default branch>`.
This goes for every workspace you search, not just the item's.
Otherwise read through git, never from the checkout.
Breaking something that works today is never an ASDF assumption.
If the design builds something new instead, the HLD says why the existing code doesn't fit.
Give Reuse, What must keep working and Edge cases a section each, under those headings.
Run the code check with the builder check, once per HLD version.
Give it the domain, each workspace with the commit the deep dive read it at, and the paths to `hld.md` and `deep-dive.md`.
writing-plans: Record planning decisions as P-numbered decisions.
Close the HLD task only when ado.hldOwned is true.
On a re-plan, archive the old plan.md and sdd\ledger.md before writing the new plan.
Every entry in the HLD's What must keep working and Edge cases sections gets a test in the plan, or the plan names the existing test that covers it.
using-git-worktrees: Worktrees may live outside asdf-context, but never inside another checkout or item artifact folder.
Branches must be under user/<userName>/, the only branches the guard lets ASDF push.
Never search the disk for code, and never clone a repo.
subagent-driven-development: Pause and ask before adding a dependency the HLD did not list.
If heartbeat fails with ASDF_LOCK_NOT_OWNER, stop at once and write nothing more.
executing-plans: Use this skill only when subagents cannot be dispatched.
If heartbeat fails with ASDF_LOCK_NOT_OWNER, stop at once and write nothing more.
requesting-code-review: Run every review skill the repo provides.
Check for over-engineering and bloat, not just bugs.
The ASDF reviewer checks that everything that worked before still works, including callers and readers the HLD doesn't list.
receiving-code-review: Mark a thread Fixed only after the fix is pushed.
finishing-a-development-branch: Set auto-complete only after ASDF's own merge checks pass.
Close the parent only if it is assigned to you and every child task is complete.
Never open a second PR for an item: reuse an active ado.prId.
Close the HLD task only when ado.hldOwned is true.
Use the returned path, not a name-only index.
do-next: Do not stop after one item.
Skip any org whose Azure DevOps MCP server is unavailable, and report it.
Skip any org without a WIQL tool, and report it.
If item-new returns ASDF_OWN_TASK, skip that id.
When signals move an item to blocked, post the blocker comment with that reason.
If item-new returns ASDF_ID_CLASH, skip that id and report it in the summary.
If heartbeat fails with ASDF_LOCK_NOT_OWNER, stop working on that item at once and write nothing more.
Never move a waiting PBI to In Progress; list it as ready to start.
